title: Regularized Machine Learning-Based Technique for Robust Wind Profile Retrieval From Single-Doppler Weather Radar Under Multicollinearity Conditions
content: Accurate estimation of wind is essential for understanding atmospheric dynamics and improving weather forecasting. The volume velocity processing (VVP) technique has been widely used to retrieve wind profiles from single Doppler weather radar (DWR) observations. The VVP technique conventionally solves the overdetermined system of equations by applying the singular value decomposition (SVD). However, the VVP approach often suffers from multicollinearity, leading to an ill-conditioned design matrix, which creates numerical instability and results in physically inconsistent or invalid wind coefficient estimates. To address these limitations, the present study proposes a machine learning-based wind retrieval framework that utilizes the ridge regression technique to stabilize the inversion by penalizing ill-conditioned solutions. In addition, a support vector machine (SVM)-based classifier is proposed that rejects ill-conditioned layers prior to the inversion, designed for computational parsimony and real-time performance. The retrieval technique has been tested and validated on the C-band DWR data from Trivandrum, India, from 2017 to 2024. The method shows strong agreement with radiosonde profiles, achieving a correlation coefficient (CC) (MAE and RMSE) of 0.905 (2.310 and 2.964 m/s) for the zonal component and 0.791 (2.141 and 2.866 m/s) for the meridional component, indicating the robust performance of the retrieval algorithm. The sensitivity analysis based on reduced  $\chi ^{2}$  thresholds shows that ridge regularization improves numerical stability while preserving error magnitudes comparable to the classical SVD approach. Furthermore, the SVM-based classifier reduces the computational workload by approximately one-third (33%), making the proposed framework suitable for near-real-time radar wind retrieval applications.
author: Vaibhav Tyagi, Saurabh Das, Abhishek Chhari, Bipasha Paul Shukla

title: Multiscale Conditional Diffusion for SST Prediction via Auxiliary Graph Learning With Future-Consistency Supervision
content: Sea surface temperature (SST) forecasting is essential for marine environmental monitoring and the early warning of extreme oceanic events. Driven by complex air–sea interactions and ocean dynamic processes, SST evolution exhibits pronounced cross-regional dependencies and multiscale spatial structures. Existing data-driven methods mainly model spatiotemporal dependencies from historical observations, making it difficult to explicitly characterize spatial associations related to future evolution. Moreover, they often lack multiscale structural constraints to guide the generation of future SST fields. To address these issues, we propose a multiscale conditional diffusion framework for SST prediction via auxiliary graph learning with future-consistency supervision. Specifically, we design an auxiliary graph learning with future-consistency supervision module, which constructs a spatiotemporal dependency graph by coupling geographical adjacency with latent structural associations learned from historical SST sequences. During training, consistency among observed future SST change trajectories is used as an auxiliary supervisory signal to encourage each anchor region to identify regions with similar future evolution patterns, while only historical observations are required during inference. Furthermore, the spatiotemporal representations encoded from the learned graph relations are transformed into multiscale conditional priors, which are progressively injected into the reverse diffusion process as hierarchical guidance to improve the generation of future SST fields. Experimental results on daily National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) optimum interpolation SST (OISST) data over China Seas and adjacent waters demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative spatiotemporal forecasting baselines.
author: Yingao Gao, Di Niu, Ning Song, Yanfeng Pan, Xinyue Liang, Min Ye, Jie Nie

title: Geometry Prior-Guided Segmentation Error Correction Method: A Case Study of Building Extraction
content: Although significant progress has been achieved in the overall accuracy of remote sensing semantic segmentation, segmentation results for high-resolution remote sensing imagery still suffer from issues, such as discontinuous boundaries and geometric structure distortion due to model errors and image noise, thereby limiting their downstream applications. To address these challenges, this study approaches the problem from the perspective of generative modeling by uniformly modeling structural deviations in semantic segmentation results as segmentation noise. Conditioned on coarse segmentation masks, we introduce edge maps and depth maps to characterize planar and 3-D geometric constraints, respectively, while textual descriptions are employed as global priors. Within a diffusion-based generative framework, iterative denoising and progressive refinement are performed to transform erroneous segmentation outputs into structurally refined results. Building semantic segmentation is taken as a representative case for methodological illustration and experimental evaluation. Experimental results on the WHU, INRIA, and Massachusetts datasets demonstrate that, compared with the segmentation outputs generated by DeepLabV3, the proposed method improves the intersection over union (IoU) by 10.78%, 8.44%, and 14.57%, respectively. Furthermore, it shows clear advantages over other optimization approaches, validating its effectiveness and robustness.
author: Hao Cui, Wei Wang, Guo Zhang, Zekun Hu, Ji Qi, Haifeng Li, Gui Gao

title: Asymmetry-Driven Synergy: Collaborative Enhancement of Visible and Infrared AAV Images via Constraint-Shaped Response Field Modeling and Correspondence-Woven Reciprocal Learning
content: Autonomous aerial vehicles (AAV)-borne visible and infrared sensors provide complementary spectral observations for remote sensing under complex acquisition conditions. However, existing visible–infrared enhancement methods remain limited in reconciling cross-modal complementarity with modality-specific reconstruction objectives under heterogeneous degradations. Guided approaches depend on the fidelity of the source modality, whereas bidirectional collaboration may entangle shared structural cues with degradation-specific responses, compromising the intended benefits of cross-modal interaction. To address these limitations, we propose an adaptive multimodal collaborative enhancement (AMCE) framework for joint visible image restoration and infrared image super-resolution. Dual-path filter modulation (DFM) constructs a dual-source complementary response field that translates complementary operator constraints into degradation-adaptive reconstruction through response-conditioned regulation of structural evidence and residual spatial variations. Axial reciprocal weaving (ARW) constructs a correspondence-woven reciprocal state space by interleaving spatially paired visible–infrared representations along direction-aware axial trajectories. On VGTSR2.0, AMCE achieves an average PSNR/SSIM of 33.07 dB/0.9402 for visible low-light enhancement, deblurring, and dehazing, and 35.22 dB/0.9259 for infrared  $\times 4$  super-resolution. Downstream oriented object detection further achieves an average mAP50 of 90.10% across the evaluated visible detection settings and an mAP50 of 48.20% on super-resolved infrared images, confirming improvements in reconstruction quality and downstream AAV perception.
author: Huan Wang, Gaohui Cheng, Yiwei Li, Pengju Si, Baofeng Ji, Yongming Yang

title: SSUC-CD: A Self-Supervised and Unsupervised Collaborative Framework for Automatic Change Detection in Multitemporal Remote Sensing Images
content: Automatic change detection offers the significant advantage of eliminating reliance on costly and labor-intensive manual annotation data, and has become a research hotspot in the field of remote sensing information extraction. However, existing studies typically employ self-supervised learning or unsupervised learning independently and lack self-supervised learning strategies specifically designed for change detection. To address this limitation, we propose a self-supervised and unsupervised collaborative change detection (SSUC-CD) framework, which is applicable to both homogeneous and heterogeneous remote sensing images. During each training epoch, the model first performs self-supervised learning on simulated change data, followed by unsupervised learning on real multitemporal images. First, SSUC-CD utilizes the class information in remote sensing images as the source of self-supervised signals tailored for change detection. By dynamically generating simulated change data based on the real-world multitemporal images, the model gradually learns the true ability to represent and extract change information by self-supervised learning. Second, SSUC-CD leverages unsupervised change detection learning on real-world multitemporal images to further refine the model’s change detection capability. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments were conducted across six datasets. Compared with 20 state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method significantly improves the automation level and reliability of change detection without requiring manually labeled sample data. The complete source code of this method will be made publicly available at the following website upon publication: https://github.com/huifuzhuang/SSUC-CD
author: Huifu Zhuang, Yuli Zhang, Xiang Zhang, Yu Zhang, Zhong Lu, Ming Hao, Hua Zhang, José Fernández, Sen Du

title: Imaging Influence Factors Analysis and Orbit-Driven Motion Compensation Method for Spaceborne High-Bandwidth ISAR
content: Spaceborne wideband inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) faces unprecedented challenges in space situational awareness (SSA) due to high-order spatiotemporal migration error induced by complex relative orbital dynamics and high bandwidth. To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose a novel precise motion compensation framework based on orbit-driven imaging characteristics. First, radar and orbital parameters are quantitatively linked to imaging constraints [achievable synthetic aperture period, observation angle, pulse repetition frequency, and imaging projection plane (IPP)], establishing a theoretical basis for system design. Second, slant-range curvature-based segmentation method divides the observation period into three distinct segments (approach, interaction, and departure), each segment exhibiting unique spatiotemporal characteristics. The characteristics are validated through theoretical derivations and numerical simulations, providing a reference for selecting appropriate imaging segments and designing a high-precision motion compensation algorithm. Third, leveraging these characteristics, we conduct a detailed analysis of the wavenumber-domain signal and propose a wavenumber-domain motion compensation method. Based on the provided prior information, we further present a hierarchical compensation coefficient estimation method. This method enables up to third-order error compensation and yields high-precision imaging results of the target. Finally, experimental validations demonstrate superior performance in high-precision rotation motion compensation for high-bandwidth radar.
author: Yichen Zhou, Yong Wang, Junting Yang, Wenjun Ding, Junqiu Zhang

title: A Statistical Framework for Bounded Measurements With Applications to SAR Data
content: Continuous data supported on the unit interval are common in remote sensing, yet the two main tractable models, the beta and Kumaraswamy distributions, trade flexibility for analytical convenience or vice versa. This article introduces the BFR distribution, a new two-parameter model for double-bounded data built from a generalized arctan-based mapping of the real line onto the unit interval. Its cumulative distribution function (cdf) is closed-form and easily inverted, yielding quantile-based estimators that avoid the numerical optimization that maximum likelihood estimation requires. A Monte Carlo study shows these estimators are accurate and improve with sample size, tracking the maximum likelihood estimators closely at a fraction of the computational cost. We further propose a Pearson-like diagram that classifies models using order statistic-based measures of skewness and kurtosis rather than sample moments, extending the classification to distributions whose moments may not exist. We illustrate the framework with the generalized radar vegetation index (GRVI) computed from full polarimetric RADARSAT-2 acquisitions over canola, soybean, and spring wheat fields across the 2016 growing season. The new diagram compactly captures the phenological transitions each crop undergoes, from early vegetative growth through canopy closure and senescence, showing the value of the proposed distribution and diagram for monitoring crop development from polarimetric radar data.
author: Avik Bhattacharya, Alejandro C. Frery, Andrea A. Rey

title: A Physics-Derived Loss-Aware Linear Mixing Model for Hyperspectral Unmixing With Spectral Variability
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to decompose mixed pixels into endmembers and their corresponding abundances. However, spectral variability arising from intrinsic material properties and environmental conditions introduces scaling variability that the classical linear mixing model (LMM) fails to adequately characterize. To address this, we extend the LMM by proposing a novel physics-derived framework named the loss-aware LMM (LALMM). Grounded in an absorbing Markov chain, LALMM explicitly simulates the light propagation process by introducing propagation loss and capture probability, and derives a pixel-wise scaling factor from the limiting transition matrix of the Markov chain. This formulation provides a rigorous physical interpretation of multiplicative spectral variability as a consequence of energy dissipation during light propagation, establishing a principled connection between radiative transfer physics and the scaling coefficients commonly adopted in LMM variants. To solve LALMM efficiently, we further develop the loss-aware nonnegative tensor factorization (LA-NTF) algorithm, which employs the core tensor as a structured low-rank representation of the spectral variability effects modeled by LALMM and incorporates joint spatial–spectral constraints to regularize the enlarged solution space associated with the additional latent variables. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior unmixing accuracy and robustness of the proposed LA-NTF compared to several state-of-the-art algorithms.
author: Tongshu Wu, Fanqiang Kong, Dan Li, Yunsong Li, Haocheng Yang

title: FFKAN: A Lightweight Hyperspectral Image Classification Network via Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Physically Constrained Fourier KAN
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires effective modeling of complex spectral–spatial variations while suppressing spectral redundancy and maintaining computational efficiency. Existing frequency-domain methods often use fixed transformations, while Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN)-based approaches typically serve as generic nonlinear modules, leaving HSI-specific frequency characteristics insufficiently explored. To address these limitations, this article proposes FFKAN, a lightweight frequency-aware network that integrates learnable 3-D wavelet decomposition with a physically constrained Fourier Kolmogorov–Arnold representation. First, a learnable 3-D wavelet frequency decomposition (FD) module (L3D-WFDM) decomposes the input into multiple spectral–spatial subbands, allowing low-frequency structural information and high-frequency discriminative details to be jointly captured. The resulting subbands are aggregated into compact representations and enhanced by 3-D positional encoding. Subsequently, a physically constrained Fourier KAN (PC-FKAN) module combines residual 3-D spatial context enhancement with learnable Fourier basis functions to efficiently model nonlinear spectral–spatial dependencies. Experiments on the Pavia University, Salinas, Xuzhou, and WHU-Hi-HanChuan datasets demonstrate that FFKAN achieves competitive classification performance with fewer parameters and lower computational complexity than several state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness and lightweight design.
author: Dongtao Mo, Xiaoqing Wan, Genping Zhao, Huilu Tang, Zhize Li

title: GeoFGA: Fine-Grained Image–Text Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
content: Open-vocabulary remote sensing image semantic segmentation (OVRSIS) leverages pretrained vision–language models to align visual features with textual semantics in a shared embedding space, enabling pixel-level recognition of both seen and unseen classes. Despite this capability, existing methods often struggle to preserve reliable image–text alignment for dense prediction. Ambiguous class semantics and interference from adjacent land-cover regions further distort dense image–text correlations, leading to erroneous activations and class confusion. To address these issues, we propose GeoFGA, a fine-grained image–text alignment framework for OVRSIS. Specifically, we introduce a Geospatial Attribute-Guided Text Enhancement (GATE) module, which organizes large language model (LLM)-generated category descriptions into a shared attribute prototype space and utilizes image-conditioned attribute composition to capture context-aware and discriminative geospatial semantics. Furthermore, a Hierarchical Correlation Recalibration (HCR) strategy is proposed to refine dense image–text correlations through spatial, feature, and category reliability recalibration with GATE-enhanced textual features, thereby enhancing adaptability in remote sensing scenarios. Extensive experiments on seven remote sensing datasets demonstrate that GeoFGA achieves the best average performance among the compared methods and improves the discrimination of unseen classes.
author: Miao Hui, Lina Xiong, Hang Yao, Xiaoqiang Li, Xinpeng Zhang

title: An Improved Ionospheric Tomography Method Based on a Dynamic Hybrid Grid and Weighted Constraint Strategy Considering Ray Distribution
content: Ionospheric tomography reconstruction based on the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) techniques has been widely applied in recent years to monitor ionospheric fluctuations with high spatial and temporal resolution. However, many grid cells are not able to be updated over time as a result of lacking observations due to uneven distribution of rays, making the performance of tomography highly dependent on the initial values. Furthermore, the constraint strategies that have been widely applied do not take into account the relationship between the ray distribution and the constraint strategy, which would further degrade the performance of tomography. To address these two limitations, we propose an improved ionospheric tomography method based on a dynamic hybrid grid and a weighted constraint strategy considering the distribution of rays (HWCR). A hybrid-grid strategy mitigates the influence of uneven ray distribution, while a weighted constraint strategy enhances the accuracy of ionospheric tomography. Based on the International Reference Ionosphere 2020 (IRI-2020) model, both simulation and real data ionospheric tomography experiments are conducted over Zhejiang Province, China, at four different time epochs. In the simulation experiments, the results show that the proposed method achieves an average improvement of approximately 31.01% in mean absolute error (MAE) and 30.01% in root-mean-square error (RMSE) compared to three traditional methods. In the real data experiments, the average improvements are about 17.21% in MAE and 14.94% in RMSE, respectively. Moreover, comparison with the Constellation Observing System for Meteorology, Ionosphere, and Climate-2 (COSMIC-2) radio-occultation data shows that HWCR provides better agreement around the F-layer peak region. Thus, both simulation and real data experiment results confirm the feasibility and superiority of the proposed method.
author: Mingkun Su, Tingyao Xie, Wei Lin, Yan Chen, Changsheng Cai, Yang Gao, Qicheng Sun, Chengdong Li

title: Seismic Inversion Method Based on Anisotropic Spatial–Structure Kriging With Autocorrelation Parameters of Random Media
content: Subsurface media generally exhibit heterogeneity and anisotropic characteristics. The assumption that the spatial structure of subsurface media is isotropic does not conform to the actual spatial–structural features of subsurface media. Considering the varying trends of spatial data in different directions, this article integrates random media theory with the simple Kriging method to establish an anisotropic spatial–structure Kriging interpolation method based on statistical characteristic parameters. First, logging data and seismic data are utilized to estimate the statistical characteristic parameters, which are employed to calculate the spatial correlation lengths and covariance functions of the subsurface medium in various directions, thereby yielding Kriging interpolation results that better match the actual spatial–structural characteristics of the subsurface medium. Furthermore, this article incorporates the Kriging interpolation results into the inversion objective function based on Bayesian theory. By using the (quantum annealing) QA-(Markov chain Monte Carlo) MCMC inversion algorithm, perturbation updates are performed on the objective function to obtain inversion solutions that satisfy the posterior distribution. Through comparative experiments with the traditional Kriging interpolation method, model tests and real data applications demonstrate that the Kriging interpolation results obtained by the proposed method more closely conform to the actual anisotropic spatial–structural characteristics of the subsurface medium. The inversion results exhibit clearer thin layers and better lateral continuity, further verifying the feasibility and practicality of the method presented in this article.
author: Baoli Wang, Yongqiang Tan, Jianwu Sun, Guangzhi Zhang, Xingyao Yin

title: SARShipRES: A Scattering-Aware Dataset and Structure-Regularized Framework for Referring SAR Ship Segmentation
content: Accurately localizing and segmenting user-specified ships in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is essential for maritime surveillance, traffic monitoring, and interactive ocean observation. Referring expression segmentation (RES) provides a flexible language-guided paradigm for target selection; however, existing RES methods are mainly developed for natural images and are difficult to directly transfer to SAR scenarios due to the scattering-dominated imaging mechanism, speckle noise, cluttered nearshore backgrounds, and ambiguous object boundaries. Moreover, most existing RES datasets assume a one-to-one correspondence between an expression and a single target, which is inconsistent with practical maritime interpretation, where a user may refer to multiple ships sharing similar spatial or scattering properties. To address these issues, we present SARShipRES, a SAR-specific referring ship segmentation dataset that integrates spatial, area, semantic, and scattering-aware descriptions and supports both one-to-one and one-to-many image–text–mask annotations. Based on this dataset, we propose a SAM-based multimodal segmentation framework tailored to SAR imaging characteristics. The proposed method introduces a decoder-level scatter-suppressed topological mask refinement strategy to reduce nonstructural bright scatterers, enhance region connectivity, and alleviate fragmented predictions. In addition, an adaptive boundary-aware shape regularization scheme is designed to improve boundary smoothness and geometric consistency while avoiding overregularization of small targets. Extensive experiments under both inshore and offshore conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative RES baselines.
author: Yixuan Lv, Furui Chen, Zhuang Zhou, Han Wang, Yuxuan Liu, You Song

title: Open-Set Domain Generalization via Spectral–Spatial Uncertainty Disentanglement for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Open-set domain generalization (OSDG) aims to classify known samples and reject previously unseen classes in a target domain that is unavailable during training. For hyperspectral images, acquisition changes and novel materials can alter the same spectral measurements, making the two effects difficult to distinguish. An OSDG framework with separate spectral and spatial pathways whose uncertainties are estimated by evidential deep learning is proposed. The proposed spectral–spatial uncertainty disentanglement mechanism combines these estimates according to their samplewise reliability. The lower uncertainty pathway determines the base estimate, while a reduced contribution from the other pathway is intended to preserve complementary evidence of novelty. Spectrum-invariant frequency disentanglement is used to reduce acquisition-dependent spectral variation, and a dual-channel residual network maintains separate spectral and spatial representations before fusion. Across the Pavia University (PU)–Pavia Center (PC), Houston 2013–Houston 2018, and Dioni–Loukia benchmarks, the best HOS on PU–PC and the second-best HOS on the other two tasks are achieved by the proposed method, although unlabeled target data are used during training by the competing open-set domain adaptation methods.
author: Amirreza Khoshbakht, Erchan Aptoula

title: FDBGF-Net: Frequency-Decoupled Bidirectional Gated Fusion for Infrared–Visible Object Detection Under Degradation in UAV Imagery
content: Infrared–visible fusion is increasingly used to improve object detection robustness in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. However, real-world UAV imagery is often affected by co-occurring degradations, such as blur, rain, snow, fog, strong illumination, and electromagnetic interference. These disturbances may simultaneously corrupt both modalities, weaken cross-modal complementarity, and make conventional fusion schemes unreliable. To address this problem, we propose FDBGF-Net, a frequency-decoupled bidirectional gated fusion network for infrared–visible object detection under compound degradation. The proposed framework introduces three coordinated components. First, a dual-modal gated fusion network performs P3-level cross-modal alignment through selective state-space modeling, preserving geometric details before high-level semantic compression. Second, a degradation-aware gated fusion network employs a bidirectional gated feature pyramid and a spatial adaptive router to dynamically aggregate multiscale features according to modality reliability. Third, a Wavelet-Decoupled Frequency Attention module separates fused representations into low-frequency structural and high-frequency detail components, and adaptively recalibrates their contributions using dual-path channel gating. We also construct a benchmark containing 3711 infrared–visible image pairs, five target categories, six degradation types, and three severity levels. Experimental results show that FDBGF-Net achieves 79.8% mAP$_{50}$ on the proposed benchmark, outperforming DPAL-R by 1.5 percentage points at 76.3 FPS. It also reaches 79.6% mAP$_{50}$ on VEDAI and 88.1% mAP$_{50}$ on aligned FLIR after independent target-dataset retraining, demonstrating consistent cross-dataset applicability across substantially different data distributions.
author: Kaipeng Wang, Guanglin He, Zongze Li, Xiaoyan Zheng, Hao Zhang

title: JASTFR-Net: Joint Attention-Based Spatio-Temporal Feature Reconstruction Network for Multiframe Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection plays a crucial role in a variety of remote sensing-related applications, such as maritime rescue, forest fire prevention, and precision guidance. However, the small size and weak intensity of infrared small targets, coupled with complex background clutter, make discriminative feature extraction difficult. Recent single-frame methods have substantially improved spatial feature learning for infrared small target detection. Nevertheless, methods based on an individual frame may remain vulnerable to target-like clutter and low-contrast backgrounds because they cannot exploit interframe consistency. Therefore, in this article, we propose a joint attention-based spatio-temporal feature reconstruction network, called JASTFR-Net, for multiframe infrared small target detection. First, a convolutional long short-term memory module based on a joint attention mechanism (JAconvLSTM) is fully exploited. By incorporating a joint attention mechanism into a temporal long short-term memory, the ability of detection network to extract spatial features of small targets is enhanced. Then, we design an edge-refined spatio-temporal feature reconstruction module for the purpose of enhancing spatio-temporal representation and accurate infrared small target segmentation in complex backgrounds. Specifically, a 3-D encoder module encodes the spatio-temporal feature map output by the JAconvLSTM module, extracting multiscale feature information layer by layer. Temporal weighted aggregation learns normalized weights for the relative frame positions and uses them to fuse the temporal features, after which a 2-D decoder restores the spatial locations and details. Besides, edge gradient information is introduced to optimize the feature reconstruction results, which further improves the ability to restore small target details. Experimental results show that our presented JASTFR-Net improves the intersection over union and $F_{1}$-measure scores by 5.34% and 3.30%, and 3.48% and 2.98% on the public NUDT-MIRSDT and TSIRMT datasets compared to the suboptimal method.
author: Minjie Wan, Fubin Chu, Xiaofang Kong, Weixian Qian, Guohua Gu, Qian Chen

title: Turning Motion Offset From Liability to Asset: TSE-RD for GEO–LEO SAR Ship Localization
content: Reliable and high-precision localization of ships in remote ocean areas remains a critical yet challenging demand for maritime safety and global shipping management. The distributed configuration of geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (SAR) illuminator and low Earth orbit SAR receiver offers a promising architecture for persistent, wide-area maritime remote sensing. However, the accurate localization of moving ships remains challenging due to the inherent failure of the classical range–Doppler (RD) model, compounded by significant multisource observation errors. To address these issues, this article proposes a time-series-enhanced RD localization method. By establishing an offset transfer model across multiple frames to jointly estimate target position and velocity, it effectively overcomes the failure problem of the classical RD model. Furthermore, this article systematically models various error sources, including atmospheric delays, orbital determination errors, and time–frequency synchronization errors, and derives the Cramér–Rao lower bound for localization accuracy. Simulation results indicate that under the four-frame joint localization, the system achieves a tangential accuracy better than 500 m with a total synthetic aperture time of 10 s. Experimental validation based on airborne–ground bistatic SAR further demonstrates that the proposed method can attain a localization accuracy better than 60 m, significantly improving accuracy compared to traditional single-frame approaches.
author: Jiayu Fu, Yuanhao Li, Feifeng Liu, Zhiyang Chen, Junhua Tian, Xiaodong Zang, Cheng Hu

title: Deep Spectral Super-Resolution via Fourier Phase Prior and Spectral Degradation Guidance
content: Spectral super-resolution (SSR) aims to reconstruct high-fidelity hyperspectral images from low-resolution RGB or multispectral images. Existing methods often struggle to balance global spectral consistency and local spatial details, frequently overlooking the loss of structural information during reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose a deep SSR network via Fourier phase prior and spectral degradation guidance. By utilizing the half-quadratic splitting algorithm, we decouple the highly coupled objective function into three alternately optimized subproblems: spectral degradation and phase guidance, spectral low-rank projection, and deep prior, which are then unfolded into an end-to-end network. Specifically, the spectral degradation and phase guidance stage introduces a Fourier phase-amplitude mixing strategy, fusing the phase prior of the multispectral image with the feature amplitude from the previous stage. This enables the image reconstruction process to adhere to the spectral response function constraint while preserving clear structural contours. The spectral low-rank stage employs truncated singular value decomposition to project data into a low-dimensional clean subspace, effectively suppressing spectral distortion and noise. Furthermore, the deep prior stage adopts a dual-branch architecture. One branch, the bidirectional spectral fusion module, connects forward spectral multihead self-attention and backward multiscale 1-D convolutions in parallel, achieving comprehensive bidirectional mining of both global correlations and local details within the spectral sequence. The other branch utilizes orientation texture-aware attention, integrating learnable directional Gabor filters and coordinate features to precisely reconstruct the high-frequency texture structures of complex scenes. Experiments on natural and remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the proposed method effectively overcomes the limitations of single spatial–spectral mapping, achieving superior performance in both spatial texture recovery and spectral fidelity.
author: Pengyue Zhang, Donge Zhao, Yayun Ma, Wenbo Chu

title: Ocean Front Prediction With a Spatiotemporal Hybrid Deep Network
content: Accurate prediction of ocean front evolution is critical for climate research, marine ecosystem management, and underwater acoustic applications, yet remains exceptionally challenging due to the multiscale, nonlinear, and strongly coupled spatiotemporal dynamics inherent in mesoscale processes. This article investigates a domain-specific formulation for ocean front forecasting, namely structure-aware residual prediction of the SST-gradient field (Ocean Front Prediction Network, OFPNet). The formulation is implemented using established spatial, temporal, feature-fusion, and structural-loss components, whose roles are coordinated to test this hypothesis. A gated convolutional long short-term memory with dual memory states is designed to enhance the model‘s capacity for capturing information across multiple temporal scales, and a cross-attention-based fusion mechanism that adaptively integrates spatial and temporal representations. To overcome the limitations of conventional pixelwise loss functions in frontal zone characterization, a multicomponent loss strategy is introduced, combining gradient loss, frontal structure similarity loss, and total variation regularization to jointly optimize numerical accuracy, morphological fidelity, and edge sharpness. Extensive experiments conducted on Moving MNIST and two satellite-derived sea surface temperature datasets (OISST and JCOPE2M) demonstrate that OFPNet achieves highly competitive performance against competitive performance against the evaluated spatiotemporal baselines spatiotemporal prediction models. Specifically, OFPNet demonstrates clear advantages in numerical accuracy (RMSE, MAE) and global morphological fidelity (Hu Similarity), underscoring its superior capability to preserve the complex geometry. Notably, OFPNet achieves substantial improvements in structural similarity and Hu moment invariance metrics, underscoring its superior capability to preserve the complex geometry and continuity of thermal fronts over forecasting horizons up to seven days. While true ocean front dynamics are governed by multiphysics processes, and the current results do not yet demonstrate a physically consistent ocean front forecasting system, the proposed framework offers a robust, structurally-aware, data-driven approach for forecasting the kinematic evolution of sea surface temperature fronts. It is important to clarify that OFPNet directly predicts the continuous SST gradient magnitude field (a gridded scalar field representing frontal intensity at each pixel) from which discrete frontal structures are subsequently extracted via a postprocessing pipeline. Our framework is, therefore, best characterized as gradient-field prediction with structure-aware optimization, rather than an explicit front-dynamics simulator that predicts the trajectories, births, and deaths of individual fronts. This distinction shapes both our methodological design and evaluation strategy.
author: Xiang Wan, Lei Zhang, Maolin Li, Xiaodong Ma, Weishuai Xu

title: SSPNet: Spatial-Semantic Foundation Prior Network for Remote Sensing Few-Shot Segmentation
content: Few-shot segmentation seeks to identify and delineate target objects in a query image with the guidance of only a handful of annotated support samples. While considerable progress has been made on natural image benchmarks, applying these techniques to remote sensing imagery remains challenging due to the pronounced intraclass appearance diversity and the pervasive spectral confusion between foreground and background. In this article, we propose a spatial-semantic foundation prior network (SSPNet) that harnesses two heterogeneous frozen foundation models to address these difficulties. SSPNet comprises a dual-stream multimodal semantic fusion (DMSF) module and a dynamic class activation map (CAM)-guided mask-aware cross-attention (DCMA) module. The DMSF module employs a frozen DINOv2 encoder and a frozen GeoRSCLIP text encoder whose representations originate from different pretraining objectives; a learnable cross-modal projection maps the language representation into the spatial feature space, enabling complementary spatial and semantic CAMs to be constructed in a shared hidden space. The DCMA module then incorporates the fused activation prior through bounded residual modulation and foreground-constrained cross-attention. An auxiliary pseudomask objective provides a downstream-to-prior gradient pathway through the learnable activation-generation and feature-refinement layers, coupling their optimization during episodic training. Experiments on the iSAID-5$^{i}$ and LoveDA-2$^{i}$ benchmarks show that SSPNet achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across the evaluated settings, with the most pronounced improvements under the one-shot protocol.
author: Yi Zhong, Guodong Zhao

title: Graph and Attention-Based Convolutional Network for Polarimetric SAR Image Classification
content: In a polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification task, exploring polarimetric-spatial relationships among the given pixel with other classes is of high importance. Moreover, providing a rich source of global and local polarimetric, scattering, and contextual features is essential to achieve a high accurate classification map. To address these issues, a graph- and attention-based convolutional (GAC) network is designed in this work. To explore the relationships among the input patch with the mean patches of all classes, a graph branch with a correlation-based feature matrix and a learnable adjacency matrix is constructed, which leads to global feature extraction. To extract the relationships among the input patch with physical scattering characteristics of all classes, a cross-attention-based convolutional branch is designed to extract the local contextual features weighted by attended scattering properties. The extracted local and global features are finally fused and used for PolSAR image classification. The experimental results on synthetic and real benchmark datasets show superior performance of GAC with less number of model parameters compared to some state-of-the-art models.
author: Maryam Imani, Sergio Escalera

title: Adversarial Patch Attack on Ship Detection via Localized Data Augmentation
content: Current ship detection techniques based on remote sensing imagery primarily rely on the object detection capabilities of deep neural networks (DNNs). However, DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial patch attacks, which can deceive the detection model and lead to misclassifications. Numerous studies have demonstrated that data augmentation-based methods can improve the transferability of adversarial patches. However, excessive augmentation of image backgrounds or irrelevant regions may introduce unnecessary interference, which also resulting in false detections of the detection models. When using such kind of loss to optimize the adversarial patches, it will inevitably lead to the optimization direction deviating from correct track, because these loss are not caused by the adversarial patches themselves but rather by the overaugmentation of background and nontarget areas. Therefore, this article proposes a localized data augmentation method that applies augmentation only to the target regions, avoiding any influence on nontarget areas. By reducing background interference, this approach enables the loss function to focus more directly on the impact of the adversarial patches on the detection model, thereby improving the attack success rate. Experiments conducted on the HRSC2016 dataset have confirmed our hypotheses. When compared with the baselines, including the global data augmentation based method, the proposed method shows the ability to increase the attack success rate of adversarial patches and enhance their transferability across different object detection models.
author: Chun Liu, Panpan Ding, Zheng Zheng, Hailong Wang, Bingqian Zhu, Tao Xu, Guangxia Wang

title: FusionGaussian: Incremental 3-D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Aerial Photogrammetry
content: Large-scale unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry is essential for geospatial modeling, where 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) has recently shown transformative potential for high-fidelity reconstruction. However, existing 3DGS frameworks for large-scale scenes often rely on static partitioning and lack the flexibility needed for incremental expansion. When updating models with multimission data, these methods incur prohibitive computational costs for global retraining and exhibit geometric inconsistencies at fusion boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose FusionGaussian, a novel framework for scalable and incremental scene reconstruction based on 3DGS. Our approach enables independent training of subscenes captured from different UAV missions and supports incremental integration without global retraining. Specifically, we incorporate an overlap-aware view selection and boundary refinement strategy to address insufficient supervision in boundary regions, along with a blockwise competitive merging mechanism to improve rendering quality and geometric consistency during scene fusion. Extensive experiments on four real-world UAV datasets and two temporal update case studies demonstrate that FusionGaussian consistently outperforms direct-merge incremental baselines in rendering and geometric quality, particularly in overlapping regions, while achieving competitive full-scene quality and substantially lower cumulative reconstruction cost than repeated Global-All reconstruction.
author: Zhenyu Xia, Pengcheng Han, Lin Chen, Boni Hu, Shuhui Bu

title: Expert-Instruction and Quality-Assessment Guided Refinement of Binary Geo-Entity Masks via Latent Rectified Flow
content: Automatic extraction of binary geo-entity masks from remote sensing imagery is fundamental to a wide range of geo-spatial tasks. Nevertheless, even advanced segmentation networks frequently produce outputs marred by boundary irregularities, merging of adjacent instances, and structural fragmentation. Typical mask optimization approaches are often constrained: hand-crafted algorithms suffer from limited transferability across scenes, while learning-based methods are usually embedded within specific architectures, hindering their reusability. To bridge this gap, we introduce OptimFlow, a decoupled refinement framework that reformulates mask optimization as a multicondition image editing task. Built upon a latent rectified flow architecture, OptimFlow synergizes two complementary conditions to guide the refinement process: category-level expert instructions in natural language that offer global semantic priors over the optimization process, and a panoramic quality assessment map that provides pixelwise spatial guidance by pinpointing correct and erroneous regions. Furthermore, we introduce a confidence-based voting strategy to suppress the granular noise often produced by generative models on low-entropy binary masks. Extensive experiments across building, water, and road datasets demonstrate that OptimFlow consistently improves both mask-level and geometry-level accuracy over various segmentation models. These results indicate that our approach can serve as a flexible postprocessing solution for binary mask refinement.
author: Bingnan Yang, Mingjun Peng, Zhan Zhang, Jianya Gong, Mi Zhang

title: FireAURA-Net: Progressive Candidate-Aware Representation and Localization for Tiny Forest-Fire Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
content: Detecting tiny forest fire points in remote sensing imagery is challenging due to their low pixel occupancy, weak responses, irregular boundaries, and similarity to fire-like woodland backgrounds. Limited task-specific training data further exacerbate representation insufficiency and foreground–background imbalance. In this article, we propose an adaptive unified response alignment network for tiny forest-fire detection (FireAURA-Net), a lightweight detector. Local-context contrast-guided response mining preserves weak candidates through local-context contrast, shallow spatial guidance, and sparse top-$k$ selection. HSV–Semantic Heterogeneous Representation Collaborative Fusion exploits the consistency and discrepancy between an explicit HSV color prior and candidate semantic responses to improve candidate reliability under fire-like interference. Candidate-localization consistency-guided selective localization refinement block establishes bidirectional interaction between fine-grained candidate cues and deep localization semantics for cross-level refinement. Adaptive dual-cue dynamic reweighting combines target-scale and high-response background cues with weight ramp-up and a batch-level budget constraint to stabilize classification under foreground sparsity. Among the compared methods, FireAURA-Net achieves the highest $\text{AP}$, $\text{AP}_{75}$, and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.193, 0.091, and 0.149, respectively, on forest imagery for remote sensing evaluation of small fire targets, and the highest $\text{AP}_{75}$ and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.669 and 0.418, respectively, on UAVs-FFDB. These results demonstrate competitive overall detection performance and consistent advantages in detection at $\text{IoU}=0.75$ and in small-scale fire-point detection. Ablation experiments further support the modules' contributions.
author: Yuhan Liu, Hongyang Zhao, Tao Jiang, Jiayi Sun, Yi Liu, Jing Jin

title: Mapping Boreal Forest Canopy Height in Northeast China by Synergistic Use of LT-1 InSAR and GEDI LiDAR Data
content: China's L-band LuTan-1 (LT-1) satellite constellation can acquire single-pass bistatic interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) data with an appropriate spatial baseline, effectively avoiding temporal decorrelation while providing the vertical sensitivity associated with forest volume decorrelation. However, its routine single-baseline and single-polarization observation configuration could render forest canopy height inversion underdetermined by using traditional coherent scattering models. Aiming at this problem, we here propose a new method of forest canopy height retrieval from bistatic LT-1 InSAR data based on a simplified volume decorrelation model constrained by global ecosystem dynamics investigation (GEDI) LiDAR observations. Instead of adopting fixed empirical parameters, spatiotemporally matched GEDI RH98 canopy height samples were used to separately calibrate the vertical scattering scale parameter and coherence correction parameter for four LT-1 interferometric pairs over the boreal forests of the Greater Khingan Mountains. The results show that the relationship between LT-1 coherence magnitude and the product of vertical wavenumber and GEDI forest height can be well described by the C-SINC model, yielding R2 values ranging from 0.435 to 0.569. The obtained canopy height mosaic agrees well with airborne LiDAR reference values, with an RMSE of 3.89 m and a bias of 1.30 m, outperforming the Meta CHMv2 product with an RMSE of 5.48 m and a bias of −4.30 m.
author: Pengyuan Tan, Lu Zhang, Jiali Hou, Carlos López-Martínez, Peng Shen, Chuanjun Wu, Mingsheng Liao

title: The Cooling Effects of Blue-Green Spaces in Arid Oasis Cities from an Energy Balance Perspective: A Case Study of Yinchuan, China
content: Blue-green spaces (BGS) provide effective cooling through evapotranspiration, yet the quantitative relationship between latent heat flux (LE) and cooling efficiency remains unclear, particularly in arid urban environments. Here, we quantify the cooling effects associated with instantaneous latent heat flux over BGS and identify critical thresholds governing the Cooling Energy Conversion Rate (CECR). Yinchuan, a typical arid oasis city, was selected as the study area. Multitemporal Landsat data from 2000 to 2025 were used to estimate latent heat flux (LE) based on the two-source energy balance model. Piecewise linear regression combined with partial dependence plots was applied to detect cooling thresholds and quantify CECR. In addition, an XGBoost-SHAP framework was employed to assess the relative contributions of meteorological drivers and spatial morphology of BGS. We demonstrate a significant negative correlation between LE and land surface temperature (LST) (p < 0.05), which supports the cooling effect of LE. The segmented regression further reveals the threshold at which cooling efficiency declines. The identified LE thresholds for vegetation and water bodies are 309.2 W/m2 and 430.0 W/m2, respectively, beyond which further increases in LE are associated with limited additional cooling. The corresponding maximum CECR values are 0.0361°C/(W/m2) for vegetation and 0.0585°C/(W/m2) for water bodies. The contribution of meteorological factors far outweighs that of the spatial morphology of the BGS. Net radiation is the most important predictor, contributing 41.5% and 44.7% to the cooling effects of vegetation and water bodies, respectively. These findings provide a quantitative framework for evaluating the tradeoff between evapotranspiration water(energy) consumption and instantaneous surface cooling benefits of BGS, and offer practical guidance for optimizing urban thermal mitigation strategies in water-limited regions.
author: Shubao Zhang, Feng Yang, Junming Yang, Xueyi Zhang, Junyao Li, Hailong Yu, Xianbao Su, Yanwei Wang, Yonglong Cai, Junwei Guo, Yuxiang Zhang, Xiangyang Yang, Bo Wang

title: ADST-Net: Adaptive Dual-Expert Refinement and Structure-Guided Temporal Modeling Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection aims to identify changed regions from bitemporal remote sensing images. Although deep learning-based methods have achieved remarkable progress, accurate detection remains challenging in complex scenes due to pseudochanges caused by imaging-condition variations, background texture disturbance, and insufficient structural consistency of bitemporal representations. To address these issues, this article proposes ADST-Net. The proposed network first refines single-temporal multiscale features through an adaptive dual-expert residual refinement module, which adaptively integrates local-detail modeling and large-kernel structural-context modeling before temporal comparison. Then, a structure-guided temporal difference modeling module organizes explicit temporal differences into more discriminative change representations. Finally, a progressive decoder reconstructs high-resolution binary change maps. On LEVIR-CD, SYSU-CD, and UAV-CD, ADST-Net achieves F1 scores of 91.71%, 83.93%, and 76.99%, respectively. These results, together with the ablation studies, indicate that the proposed refine-then-model strategy improves change detection accuracy while keeping the model lightweight.
author: Yang Zhang, Jintao Xu, Yijun Zhou

title: A Physical Prior-Informed Framework for Joint Detection and Suppression of Radio Frequency Interference in SAR Amplitude Images
content: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems have been increasingly subjected to severe radio frequency interference (RFI), which has led to significant degradation in imaging quality and hindered the effective utilization of ground range detected products. However, existing deep learning-based RFI suppression methods often suffer from the loss of texture detail information, insufficient preservation of salient targets, and limited physical interpretability. To address these issues, we first establish the signal and image model for diverse RFI patterns in the image domain. Based on this, we propose PPRNet, a physical prior-informed framework for joint detection and suppression. Specifically, an adaptive subspace projection layer is developed to physically isolate blanket jamming by exploiting the low-rank singular value characteristics of the interference subspace. Concurrently, a shallow jamming detector is designed to precisely localize interference regions through statistical power anomaly detection across multiple spatial dimensions. A multistage progressive target reconstruction subnetwork then integrates these physical priors to recover obscured terrain textures. Experiments on Sentinel-1 and airborne platforms validate the effectiveness of PPRNet, yielding a 14.51 dB peak signal to noise ratio improvement in specific interference scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework exhibits superior performance in suppressing various RFI types, thereby achieving high-quality, interference-free SAR imagery.
author: Lin Nie, Dongfang Guan, Keli Huang, Shuowei Liu, Zhen Liu, Yong-xiang Liu

title: Stable Feature Graph Similarity for Air–Ground Multiview 3-D Point Cloud Fusion Mapping in Confined Spaces
content: Uncrewed aerial vehicle-borne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is increasingly used for near-ground Earth observation and3-D geospatial data acquisition because of its rapid deployment and broad coverage. However, aerial platforms often provide sparse observations and may suffer from occlusion or limited accessibility in narrow, low-clearance, and obstacle-rich environments. Ground mobile platforms acquire denser close-range geometry but remain constrained by local occlusion, limited viewpoints, and poor visibility of elevated structures. Their complementary viewpoints therefore benefit confined-space mapping. Nevertheless, fusing heterogeneous air–ground point clouds remains challenging because differences in sensing height, viewpoint, field of view, point density, and spatial overlap make cross-platform place recognition and alignment unreliable. To address this problem, this article proposes an air–ground multiview point cloud fusion method based on stable feature graphs. Repeatable planar and high-intensity structures are extracted from LiDAR-inertial keyframe submaps to construct compact feature graphs. A graph similarity network, termed the graph-level interaction and subgraph cross-attention network, combines graph-level embedding interaction with label-specific subgraph cross-attention to identify overlapping regions between aerial and ground observations. Retrieved candidates are geometrically verified, and their relative poses are estimated using RANSAC and generalized iterative closest point registration. Verified cross-platform constraints are integrated with single-platform odometry through offline partitioned pose graph optimization to generate a globally consistent fused map. Experiments on multiple underground parking-garage sequences show that the proposed method improves cross-platform place-recognition performance by 16.6% over the second-best method, while also achieving better air–ground alignment, more complementary spatial coverage, and improved global map consistency.
author: Haonan Chen, Kunhuang Liu, Xing Zhang, San Jiang, Qingquan Li

title: An Adaptive Endmember-Corrected Mixing Model for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: The linear mixing model (LMM) remains a widely used foundation for hyperspectral unmixing because of its simplicity and physical interpretability. In practical scenes, however, nonlinear (NL) interactions, endmember variability (EV), and other complex factors may cause the observed spectra to deviate from the LMM, resulting in model mismatch. Existing methods address model mismatch by introducing predefined NL or EV formulations, which may lack flexibility when the mismatch source is unknown or difficult to characterize. To address this issue, this article proposes an endmember-corrected mixing model that compensates for dominant mismatch-induced spectral deviations through a compact correction to the endmember representation. Specifically, an endmember correction term is introduced into the LMM and learned by an endmember residual correction network through self-supervised reconstruction of the observed hyperspectral image. Within the adopted additive correction structure, the endmember representation can adapt to the observed data without requiring prior identification of the underlying mismatch mechanism. Meanwhile, a deep image prior network is employed to generate spatially structured abundance maps. A two-stage optimization strategy is further adopted to reduce the coupling between endmember correction and abundance estimation, thereby improving the stability of the unmixing process. Experiments on synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves robust and competitive unmixing performance under different noise levels and model mismatch conditions.
author: Jin-Ju Wang, Xi-Le Zhao, Jie Huang, Jia-Qing Miao

title: Physics-Guided Interpretable SAR Image Generation: Bridging Simulation and Reality With Explicit Geometric and Statistical Modeling
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image interpretation is limited by the scarcity of labeled measured data, especially for specific vehicle targets and observation conditions. Physics-based simulation can provide target geometry and scattering locations, but the resulting images usually lack the blur, clutter, and speckle statistics observed in measured SAR data. To address this gap, we propose PI-SAR-Net, a SAR image generation method that combines geometric simulation with a learnable rendering stage. Starting from a 3-D target model and SAR sensor parameters, an equivalent-beam-integration simulator first produces a geometry-guided SAR image. A generator then aligns the simulated image, predicts a pixelwise reflectivity map, and renders the final image with realistic blur, clutter, and speckle statistics. The observation condition vector encodes azimuth, incidence angle, and polarization, while a multitask style encoder estimates the style, speckle strength, and blur strength required for rendering from measured reference images. We construct a paired vehicle SAR dataset with simulated and measured images under matched observation conditions. Experiments show that PI-SAR-Net improves paired image fidelity, SAR-specific background statistics, and few-shot real-SAR recognition performance compared with simulation-only and image-translation baselines.
